title: A Note on Using Implicit Ratings.

cues.en: So a quick note here about implicit ratings. We talked about this a little bit earlier.
cues.zh: 這裡快速補充一下隱含評分，前面稍微談過。

cues.en: The idea that some ratings aren't really just somebody giving something an explicit five star rating or you know giving a thumbs up or thumbs down to something. Sometimes our ratings signals that we look
cues.zh: 概念是，有些評分並不是某人明確給出五星，或對某個東西按讚、倒讚。有時我們觀察的評分訊號，

cues.en: at are more implicit.
cues.zh: 比較隱含。

cues.en: So for example, somebody's clicking on a link or purchasing something.
cues.zh: 例如，某人點擊連結，或購買東西。

cues.en: Those are implicit indications of interest instead of an explicit rating.
cues.zh: 這些是隱含的興趣訊號，不是明確評分。

cues.en: And it's a common point of confusion as to how do you deal with implicit ratings versus explicit ratings.
cues.zh: 很多人會困惑，究竟該如何處理隱含評分與明確評分。

cues.en: Do you need to handle those differently?
cues.zh: 需要用不同方式處理嗎？

cues.en: How do you work with them?
cues.zh: 該如何使用？

cues.en: Well first of all I want to say that there's like a fundamental difference in how this data is used and how it's useful.
cues.zh: 首先，我想說明，這些資料的用途與有用之處，存在根本差異。

cues.en: So implicit data can often be very powerful.
cues.zh: 隱含資料往往很有力量。

cues.en: It tends to be very plentiful because you're not relying on people to interact with a widget on your website and voluntarily give you an explicit rating.
cues.zh: 它通常很充足，因為不需要仰賴使用者操作網站小工具，自願給出明確評分。

cues.en: It's just being gleaned through their actions on your Web site naturally so it tends to be very plentiful, when you're dealing with implicit data and depending on what kind of implicit data is it can actually
cues.zh: 它只是自然地從使用者在網站上的行為收集而來，所以通常很多。而且根據隱含資料的種類，

cues.en: be even more powerful and more higher quality than explicit ratings can be.
cues.zh: 它甚至可能比明確評分更有用、品質更高。

cues.en: For example, purchase-based ratings can be of extremely high quality tends to be a little bit more sparse.
cues.zh: 例如，以購買為基礎的評分，品質可能極高，雖然通常比較稀疏。

cues.en: But if somebody actually opens up their wallet and buys something that is a very strong indication of interest right, like they've actually put their money where their mouth is there.
cues.zh: 但如果有人真的打開錢包買東西，那就是非常強烈的興趣訊號，對吧？他確實用金錢支持自己的喜好。

cues.en: So you'll find that sometimes implicit ratings in the case of purchasing can actually be even higher quality than explicit ratings.
cues.zh: 因此有時，購買這類隱含評分，品質甚至比明確評分更高。

cues.en: But what do you do with that data.
cues.zh: 但該怎麼使用這些資料？

cues.en: How do you actually treat them as ratings?
cues.zh: 如何真正把它們當成評分？

cues.en: Well it turns out you can use implicit ratings just the same ways you treat explicit ratings.
cues.zh: 其實，可以用與明確評分相同的方式使用隱含評分。

cues.en: All you have to do is model a click or purchase or whatever the implicit signal is as a positive rating of some arbitrary yet consistent value.
cues.zh: 只要把點擊、購買或任何隱含訊號，建模成某個任意但一致的正面評分值。

cues.en: Maybe you treat them also rating of one or rating of five.
cues.zh: 也許全部視為一分，或全部視為五分。

cues.en: I don't care just make sure that it's some constant consistent value.
cues.zh: 我不在意，只要確保是固定、一致的數值。

cues.en: The math will typically just work out.
cues.zh: 數學運算通常自然就能成立。

cues.en: The only thing you need to be careful of is to not give into the temptation of modeling the absence of a click or purchase as a negative rating.
cues.zh: 唯一要小心的是，不要忍不住把沒有點擊或購買，建模成負面評分。

cues.en: So if somebody does not purchase something that doesn't mean that it's a zero star rating it just means that you don't know about it.
cues.zh: 某人沒有購買某個東西，不代表零星，只代表你不知道。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: They might not have bought the thing because they didn't know about it.
cues.zh: 他沒買，可能只是因為不知道那個東西。

cues.en: It doesn't mean that they're not interested in it.
cues.zh: 不代表不感興趣。

cues.en: Maybe they didn't see it at all.
cues.zh: 也許根本沒看過。

cues.en: Maybe they didn't click on it because they were not presented with that click in the first place, where they were not presented with an opportunity to purchase something in the first place.
cues.zh: 也許沒有點擊，是因為一開始根本沒向他展示可點擊的項目，或根本沒讓他有機會購買。

cues.en: So do not model the absence of an implicit rating as a negative rating.
cues.zh: 因此，絕不要把缺少隱含評分，建模為負面評分。

cues.en: It's just missing data.
cues.zh: 那只是缺失資料。

cues.en: You don't put it in your data set at all.
cues.zh: 完全不用放進資料集。

cues.en: So all you need to do is model your implicit ratings.
cues.zh: 所以，只要對隱含評分建模，

cues.en: If somebody clicks on something or purchases something whatever it might be as some positive rating and the math will generally work out the same way as if you were dealing with five star ratings as we
cues.zh: 把點擊、購買或任何這類行為，當成某種正面評分，數學運算通常就會像本課程大部分內容使用的

cues.en: typically deal with throughout this course.
cues.zh: 五星評分一樣成立。

cues.en: And again not all implicit ratings are created equal.
cues.zh: 再次強調，並非所有隱含評分都一樣。

cues.en: Purchases create very high quality recommendations it tends to be sparse sir but the data is very very good.
cues.zh: 購買資料能產生很高品質的推薦，雖然比較稀疏，但資料非常好。

cues.en: Clicks not so much.
cues.zh: 點擊就沒那麼好了。

cues.en: You know if you're dealing with implicit ratings based on clicks on a website that data can get really really messy right.
cues.zh: 如果使用網站點擊作為隱含評分，資料可能非常混亂，對吧？

cues.en: Because there's a lot of traffic coming from bots.
cues.zh: 因為很多流量來自機器人。

cues.en: A lot of people coming from you know dodgy sources from the Internet.
cues.zh: 也有很多來自網路上可疑來源的訪客。

cues.en: It's not necessarily a very good indication of interest, just because somebody visited a Web site it might not even be a person at all.
cues.zh: 光是造訪網站，不一定是很好的興趣訊號，甚至可能根本不是人。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: So keep that in mind too.
cues.zh: 這一點也要記住。

cues.en: Not all implicit ratings are created equal purchases where people are actually opening their wallet and speaking with their money tend to be very high quality implicit ratings.
cues.zh: 不是所有隱含評分都一樣。購買時，人們真的打開錢包、用金錢表態，通常是品質很高的隱含評分。

cues.en: But if there's no money on the line and nobody has anything to lose then you should question how high quality that data really is.
cues.zh: 但如果沒有花錢、沒有人會付出代價，就應該質疑資料品質究竟有多高。

cues.en: And again there's nothing special about dealing with implicit ratings versus explicit ratings. The same techniques we're talking about in this course, for a one to five-star ratings, can be applied just as
cues.zh: 再次強調，處理隱含評分與明確評分，並沒有什麼特別不同。本課程針對一到五星評分介紹的技術，也能同樣輕鬆地

cues.en: easily to implicit ratings where you just model whatever implicit signal it is at some arbitrary positive rating value.
cues.zh: 用在隱含評分，只要將任何隱含訊號，建模成任意正面評分值即可。

cues.en: It's just that easy.
cues.zh: 就是這麼簡單。

cues.en: So don't get too confused about it.
cues.zh: 所以，不用想得太混亂。
